issues.description: Default response transformer crashes on any non-JSON line; no precondition stated, no error handling
issues.detail: default_response_to_output_transformer calls json.loads(response_line) unguarded. The author has not stated the precondition on response_line. AgentCore streams 'data: ' lines that are documented to contain JSON, but the caller has already proven it does not trust this (it special-cases empty lines and warns on missing prefixes). A single malformed line — partial chunk, keep-alive comment, transport hiccup — raises JSONDecodeError out of process_frame, aborting the entire stream. Either state and enforce the precondition (line is well-formed JSON), or catch and log. The current code does neither: it relies on hope. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: SSE parsing is naive: assumes one event per network chunk and a single 'data:' field per line
issues.detail: The control flow says 'each part might have one or more lines' and splits on '\n', stripping a literal 'data: ' prefix of exactly six characters. The SSE specification permits leading whitespace variations (no space after colon, multiple data: lines coalesced into one event terminated by a blank line, CRLF line endings, event:/id:/retry: fields, comment lines beginning with ':'). The invariant 'one decoded part contains complete lines' is not stated and is not true in general: a chunk boundary may fall mid-line, in which case the trailing fragment is silently misparsed or warned away and the next chunk's leading fragment is dropped. The precondition for correct parsing is nowhere stated. SMUGGLED-GOTO: a flag (is_multi_part_response) and a continue-on-warning idiom replace what should be a proper streaming SSE state machine.

issues.description: Output-response bookend invariant is not maintained; concurrent invocations race and frames can be emitted out of order
issues.detail: State the invariant: at any pipeline-observable instant, the number of LLMFullResponseStartFrame frames pushed equals the number of LLMFullResponseEndFrame frames pushed plus (_output_response_open ? 1 : 0). This invariant is violated by construction. process_frame can be re-entered for a new LLMContextFrame while _close_task is still pending, while the previous invocation's async-for loop is still draining, or while a prior _push_text_frame is mid-flight. _output_response_open, _close_task, and _last_text_frame_time are read-modify-written without a lock or queue. Two interleaved invocations can produce Start, Start, End — or text frames after End — both of which break downstream aggregators that assume bracketed responses. The 1.0s timer is also a goto-by-clock: correctness depends on wall time rather than on a structural signal that the response is over. UNREASONED.

issues.description: AWS client is constructed per invocation inside the hot path
issues.detail: async with self._aws_session.client('bedrock-agentcore', ...) is entered on every LLMContextFrame. Client construction performs credential resolution and TLS setup; doing it per turn adds latency to every agent call and produces no benefit. The session lifetime should be the processor lifetime. This is not strictly a correctness defect, but it is the kind of sloppy resource management that the author would not have written if they had stated 'frame: what is created, what persists' before coding.

issues.description: Credentials are captured at __init__ from os.environ; rotation and refreshable credentials are silently broken
issues.detail: _aws_params snapshots AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_REGION at construction time. If the deployment uses an instance/role provider, container credential provider, or SSO with refresh, none of that machinery runs because the dict is passed positionally to the client and overrides discovery. Worse, if the env is empty at __init__, None values are passed in explicitly, which differs from omitting them entirely. State the precondition for credentials and let boto3's chain handle it, or document this restriction loudly.

issues.description: agentArn parameter violates the codebase's stated naming convention (PEP 8) without justification
issues.detail: Public Python identifiers in this file are snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_session_token, aws_region). agentArn is camelCase, presumably to mirror the AWS API field. Pick one rule and apply it: if the convention is snake_case at the Python boundary and camelCase only at the wire boundary (where it is used as agentRuntimeArn on the boto3 call), then expose agent_arn. Inconsistency here is not a vibe complaint; it is a sign the author has not decided what the abstraction boundary is.

issues.description: No exception handling around invoke_agent_runtime; one network error tears down the pipeline mid-response
issues.detail: An exception raised inside the async with after some text frames have already been pushed leaves _output_response_open == True with no End frame ever emitted. The invariant breaks and downstream consumers wait forever. DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE is not the answer either — the correct discipline is: state what must hold on every exit path (normal, exception, cancellation) and enforce it in a finally block. The current code has no finally and no story for cancellation.

issues.description: Module-level `from .agent_core import *` with no __all__ leaks helpers into the public surface
issues.detail: agent_core.py defines default_context_to_payload_transformer, default_response_to_output_transformer, AWSAgentCoreProcessor, plus imported names (asyncio, json, os, aioboto3, logger, several frame classes, LLMContext, etc.). `from .agent_core import *` exports all of them into pipecat.services.aws. State the postcondition of the import: which names are part of the API? Add __all__, or import specific names. Otherwise every transitive import becomes a backward-compatibility hazard.

issues.description: Class docstring and PR title disagree with the symbol name
issues.detail: PR title is AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor; module docstring says AWSAgentCoreProcessor; class is AWSAgentCoreProcessor. Pick the name and use it everywhere. Names are part of the specification; if the author cannot state the name consistently across the diff, the reader cannot trust that the precondition has been stated.

issues.description: default_context_to_payload_transformer ignores LLMSpecificMessage and silently returns None on non-string/non-list content
issues.detail: The transformer's stated contract is 'extracts the latest user or system message text.' Its implementation also bails on LLMSpecificMessage and on content that is dict-shaped. The list branch ' '.join(part.get('text','')...) assumes every part is a dict with a 'text' key; image/audio parts get rendered as empty strings and joined with spaces, producing payloads with runs of blank tokens. State the postcondition precisely (which message shapes are supported, what is returned for each) and either honor it or refuse the frame visibly.

issues.description: Magic constants: 6 for len('data: ') and 1.0 for the response timeout
issues.detail: line[6:] hardcodes the SSE prefix length. _output_response_timeout = 1.0 hardcodes a wall-clock window that determines correctness of the bookend invariant. Name both. The first should be a constant or a startswith-and-removeprefix; the second should be a constructor parameter so the user can reason about and tune it.

review.summary: This processor has not been reasoned about; it has been tested. The author cannot, on the evidence of the diff, state the precondition on a response line (the default transformer crashes on any non-JSON input), the invariant on the output-response bookends (Start/End balance is broken by re-entrance, the 1.0s timer, and any exception in the network path), or the frame on the AWS client lifetime (constructed per invocation). The SSE parsing is a naive split on '\\n' with a hardcoded six-character prefix and a flag-driven branch — a smuggled goto where a small state machine belongs — and assumes chunk boundaries align with line boundaries, which the protocol does not promise. The result is code that will appear to work in the demo and fail in production at the first malformed line, the first transport hiccup, the first overlapping context frame, or the first credential refresh. REFUSED until the spec, invariants, exception paths, and SSE state machine are stated and the bookend logic is restructured to be correct by construction rather than by timeout.
